# The current generated by the two particle streams

Charged particles accelerated sideways generate their own electric and magnetic fields. For two homogeneous angular patterns on the model's three-sphere, the resulting transverse currents can be evolved together with every particle momentum. In the large-source example adjusted to match the two lateral pressures, the induced fields reach **0.64% and 0.73%** of the peak supplied transverse field strength. Turning this response on changes each principal pressure by at most about two percentage points of its thermal target. Substantial differences from thermal particle counts persist.

| Case and response | Dedicated lateral pressures / target | Shared lateral pressures / target | Dedicated and shared discrepancies across 20 momentum bins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pressure-matched source, prescribed fields | 0.995, 1.005 | 0.992, 1.007 | 46.78, 55.70 percentage points |
| Same source with both induced currents | 0.982, 1.011 | 0.972, 1.017 | 47.18, 55.70 points |
| 4% early and late source with both induced currents | 0.00000065, 0.121 | 0.00000175, 0.396 | 61.90, 61.72 points |

Matching individual daughters across the feedback toggle gives median changes in flight direction of 0.0740° and 0.0649° in the pressure-fitted case, and 0.0116° and 0.0170° in the 4% early/late case. The pressure entries average the eigenvalues of the two sign-specific lateral tensors. Each tensor is local because the angular model is homogeneous. In the high-strength control, particle work creates an induced field with conformal energy 0.001451 and carries 0.0000204 out through the boundary in the dedicated history. The corresponding shared energies are 0.000975 and 0.0000189. The simulated gas has conformal energy 14.55 and 20.99, respectively. All four energy contributions have their own entries in the numerical ledger.

The high-strength control keeps the early/late amplitudes and angles of the prescribed-orbit fit. Those choices require 1,356 and 492 times the original emitted energy on the two histories, so this is a conditional test of how current affects the fitted moments. In the smaller trial each of the orthogonal early and late components has source amplitude $0.04/\sqrt{2}$. Together they add 0.16% of the original emitted energy to the original axial pulse. Their peak induced field strength is 1.17% and 1.70% of the peak supplied transverse strength. Sending both 4% components early provides a timing control. The largest principal pressure then reaches 0.243 or 0.792 of target with feedback, and both components share one rotated source waveform. ## Homogeneous Maxwell and particle equations

Use the three orthonormal invariant tangent vectors of the round shell. The first two have curl eigenvalue $-2$ and are perpendicular to the third, axial direction. Their components, the prescribed birth law and the momentum distribution are invariant under spatial translations on the group manifold. Particle momentum components are constant along the free great-circle drift. Thus all particles with the same birth time and kick history obey the same momentum equation at every position. Uniform initial positions stay uniform by the invariance. The lateral electric current is in the same two-dimensional space of fields. This makes the two transverse current equations exact within this homogeneous angular sector.

The supplied electric and magnetic coefficients come from the curved-collar, moving-boundary Maxwell calculation. We add the field of the daughter currents with zero initial induced field and fixed incoming characteristic. For conformal time $d\eta=dt/a$, horizontal conformal fields $F=a^2\delta E$ and $G=a^2\delta B$ obey
$$
 F'=-2G-\frac{2a}{K}F-\frac{1}{K}J,\qquad G'=2F,\qquad
 J=Q\sum_i w_i s_i\mathbf v_{i,\perp}.
$$
The sign is $s_i=\pm1$, $Q=10^7$ and $K=2.54$ is the constant gauge coefficient over the birth window. The two sign populations have equal mass weights. Their combined weight sums to the archived daughter rest mass $D$ per normalized volume. A unit-RMS homogeneous vector contributes a current coefficient without the factor of two used to normalize a plane-wave cosine in a periodic box. The prescribed axial mean already contains the reference gas current and supplies the axial Lorentz force throughout.

For comoving particle momentum $\mathbf u=a\mathbf p/(mc)$, conformal energy $g=\sqrt{a^2+u^2}$ and velocity $\mathbf v=\mathbf u/g$, the force is $sQ[a^2\mathbf E_{\rm supplied}+F+\mathbf v\times(a^2\mathbf B_{\rm supplied}+G)]$. Here $F,G$ are embedded as the two horizontal components. The conformal field energy is $K(|F|^2+|G|^2)/2$. Its derivative is $-J\cdot F-2a|F|^2$. The same $+J\cdot F$ enters particle work. The outgoing term is nonnegative. The index-2 conformal curl terms exchange magnetic and electric energy reversibly.

The incoming data of the *supplied* fields include the original five-dimensional propagation. The induced fields use an open wall boundary. Recomputing reflections and curvature scattering of the daughter-generated radiation in the full radial collar, evolving the axial field from the new distribution, angular metric changes and collisions lie beyond this calculation.

## Numerical checks

Both charge signs are tracked with equal positive mass weights, opposite initial kicks and their individual Sobol-sampled birth times. Newly born particles contribute current only for their occupied fraction of the first step. Symmetric magnetic rotations conserve each particle's energy at fixed $a$. Exact curl rotations and split electric damping advance the source-free induced fields. An implicit electric midpoint step uses
$$
 \mathbf v_*=(\mathbf u_{\rm before}+\mathbf u_{\rm after})/(g_{\rm before}+g_{\rm after}).
$$
This velocity enforces the exact discrete work identity. The separately accumulated birth energy, expansion contribution, imposed axial work, imposed horizontal work and induced horizontal work reproduce final particle conformal energy. Induced field energy plus outward leakage balances the energy taken by the induced current. Across the recorded cases the absolute particle residual divided by gas energy and the absolute field residual divided by induced work are both below $8\times10^{-14}$ on the reference machine. A speed-of-light upper bound $\sqrt{|F|^2+|G|^2}\le(Q/K)\int D\,d\eta$ is also checked for every discrete time sample using the actual birth weights.

A two-particle control starts opposite-sign particles drifting in opposite directions along a 3–4–5 transverse vector. For a single step the exact discrete current reduces to one scalar equation, solved independently by Brent's method. Both induced electric and both induced magnetic coefficients and the two final particle momenta agree with this control. The test exercises the sign, normalization, both horizontal currents, outgoing damping and the post-current curl rotation. Table entries use the half-step original histories, 4,096 birth pairs and 512 particle steps. Additional runs halve the particle time step at fixed tags, change tags and sample count, and repeat the calculation on the native source history. The results include energy, cumulative transverse momentum counts, large momentum cells and the angular deflection obtained by matching the same particle with feedback off and on.
```sh
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -I feedback/currents.py --history history \

```
